recommended_reasoning.reason: A bounded frontend pass with one design judgment -- drawing the two-stroke X faithfully as SVG -- and otherwise mechanical replacements; medium covers it.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'. Do not run the full Python pytest suite. The ui2 build must keep exactly eleven Gradle subprojects.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.
The SESSION_CLOSE names the two brand components, the favicon path, every file where the legacy name was removed, and the test counts before and after.
risks: Approximating the X with a plain letter instead of the two-stroke mark, which is the whole identity.
Adopting the tagline from the study because it is in the picture.
Pulling a web font to get the heavy sans, adding a dependency and an external fetch.
Renaming code identifiers 'while here' -- explicitly out of scope.

in: Produce the wordmark as an inline React SVG component (src/brand/NexusWordmark.tsx) drawn by hand from the study: the letters 'ne' and 'us' as paths or as text in a heavy geometric sans that is guaranteed present (use the theme's font stack with a bold weight; do not add a font dependency), and the capital X as two distinct strokes -- left stroke in a teal, right stroke in a blue, matching the study's two-tone X -- so the mark reads as the study's option D at every size from 20px to 200px tall. No tagline. Accept a currentColor prop for the letters so the mark works on both the light surface and a dark tile. Also produce the square icon variant (the two-stroke X alone on a dark rounded tile) as src/brand/NexusMark.tsx.

Favicon: generate an SVG favicon from the icon variant (public/favicon.svg, checked in as a static file, no build-time image tooling) and reference it from index.html; set the document title to 'neXus'. The frontend build must copy public/ into the bundle as Vite does by default -- verify the built dist contains it.

Login screen: the wordmark above the sign-in form, sized so it is the first thing seen, with the form otherwise unchanged; the h3 'Sign in' may stay as a smaller subtitle or go -- the mark carries the identity.

Shell: TopAppBar shows the wordmark (small) where the 'SecurityExpert' text was; NavigationRail shows the icon variant when collapsed and the wordmark when expanded (or whichever single form fits the rail's existing width -- do not restructure the rail). Remove every 'SecurityExpert' / 'Security Expert' string from ui2/frontend/src; a test greps the frontend sources and fails if any remains.
Every colour used comes from the theme tokens or is declared once in src/brand/ as named constants with a comment pointing at the study; nothing is hard-coded inline in the screens.

Tests: the source-grep test above; a render test for NexusWordmark and NexusMark (they render an svg with a title element 'neXus' for accessibility); LoginScreen renders the wordmark; existing tests stay green; NoRoleConditionalRenderingInFrontendTest passes.

Commit early and often (brand components; favicon + title; login; shell; tests). Open the PR at the end; do not merge. The PR body carries a summary and a test plan only -- no tool footer, no emoji, no external URL (repository owner's rule).
out: Renaming the Java package com.securityexpert.*, the Gradle root project, database objects, or any repository document (AGENTS.md, CURRENT_STATE.md) -- code-internal and governance identifiers are a separate decision, not a user-facing surface.

Any external-facing use of the mark (the LOGO row's condition); any marketing page; any change to screen layouts beyond placing the mark; any new font, image-processing or icon-generation dependency; raster assets.
Adopting the study's tagline, or any of the other five explorations.
